key_insight: High-quality biological data can make machine learning models effective quickly, but those models must be revisited as datasets change over time. The paper emphasizes that AI readiness is not a one-time state; it requires ongoing rethinking to keep models aligned with evolving data.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge of maintaining model performance and relevance when biological datasets evolve after a model has been trained. It highlights the need to update models so they remain consistent with changing data and scientific understanding.
method: Train models on high-quality biological datasets to achieve strong initial results.
Monitor dataset evolution and identify when model assumptions or performance may drift.
Re-evaluate and update models to maintain alignment with the latest data.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this reinforces that successful deployment in biology depends on continuous model maintenance, not just initial training. It helps reduce stale predictions and improves reliability in fast-moving scientific domains.
visual_elements: Timeline showing dataset evolution and periodic model updates

paper_title: Thinking and rethinking data AI readiness
